Launcher tour and short guides: profiles, Minecraft look, mods, settings
Marks every guide as new. Launcher settings, profiles and accounts are not touched.
The home screen in one minute
Where your account, profile, version, PLAY, content and settings live. Eight stops, nothing is changed.
Everything you need to play is on this one screen. Let\'s go through it — tap Next to move, Close to stop at any time.
Tap here to sign in with Microsoft or play offline with a username. Switch between saved accounts from the same menu.
A profile is a Minecraft version plus its mod loader, mods, RAM and controls. Whatever is shown here is what PLAY starts.
Choose the game version for this profile — releases, snapshots and older versions. The launcher downloads it when you press PLAY.
The pencil opens the profile editor: name and icon, version and mod loader, RAM, renderer, control layout — and the Minecraft Appearance (Vanilla or CS Custom).
One tap. Missing files are downloaded first (you\'ll see “Downloading”), then the game launches. No separate install step.
Mods, modpacks, resource packs and shaders from Modrinth and CurseForge, installed straight into the selected profile.
See what\'s installed in this profile, toggle or remove mods, and manage your worlds.
Launcher theme, performance, controls and language. The Tutorials screen (Miscellaneous → Tutorials) lets you replay this tour.
Add an account, pick a version, press PLAY. More guides — profiles, the Minecraft look, mods, settings — are in the Tutorials screen.
How profiles work, how to switch or create one, and what the profile editor controls.
Each profile keeps its own Minecraft version, mod loader, mods, RAM and controls. Keep a vanilla profile and a modded one side by side without conflicts.
This picker changes the version of the selected profile. Installed versions are kept, so switching back is instant.
Opens the profile list. Pick another profile, or create a new one and choose its version and mod loader (Fabric, Forge, NeoForge, Quilt, OptiFine).
The pencil opens the full editor for the selected profile. Next stop: inside the editor.
Name, icon and banner at the top. The rows below each open a picker — nothing is applied until you save.
Change the Minecraft version or install a mod loader for this profile. The loader is downloaded on the next PLAY.
Per-profile memory and JVM flags. Leave it on the default unless a modpack asks for more RAM.
Save applies your changes; Back discards them. The home screen shows the updated profile right away.
Minecraft look: Vanilla vs CS Custom
Original menus or the Craft Studio style
What “Minecraft Appearance” in the profile editor does, what each option changes, and the version it needs.
Two looks for the game itself
Besides the launcher theme, each profile can change how Minecraft\'s own menus look. It\'s set per profile in the editor — opening it now.
This row shows the current look of the profile and opens the chooser. Two options: Vanilla Experience and CS Custom Experience.
The original Minecraft main menu and loading screen, exactly as Mojang ships them. Nothing is added to the game.
A dark obsidian menu with platinum accents: Craft Studio title, night panorama, restyled buttons, custom splashes and a dark loading screen. You can pick which parts to apply.

CS Custom is a resource pack the launcher builds for the profile\'s version at launch and enables automatically. It needs Minecraft 1.21 or newer; on older versions the profile stays Vanilla. Game files are never modified.
Switch between the two looks whenever you like — it takes effect on the next PLAY of this profile.
How to browse Modrinth and CurseForge, filter for your version, install into a profile and manage what\'s installed.
Everything installs into the selected profile, so pick the right profile first. Opening the browser now.
Switch what you\'re looking for here. Mods need a mod loader on the profile; resource packs work everywhere; shaders need Iris or OptiFine.
Two catalogues, same flow. If something is missing on one, try the other.
Type a name, then narrow by Minecraft version and loader with the filters so results match your profile.
Open an item to read about it and choose a version; the download button installs it into the profile. Required dependencies are offered along with it.
Already have a .mrpack or CurseForge zip? Import it here — the launcher creates a profile with the right version and loader.
Back on the home screen, Manage content lists installed mods, packs, shaders and worlds for the profile — toggle, update or remove them there.
A quick map of the settings hub: which card does what, and where the Tutorials screen is.
Launcher-wide settings live behind this button; profile-specific ones (version, RAM, controls layout) are in the profile editor. Opening the hub now.
Dark, light or system theme, accent colour and animations. This is the launcher\'s look — the game\'s look is set per profile.
Renderer, resolution scale and V-Sync. Lowering the resolution scale is the quickest FPS boost on weaker phones.
Default RAM allocation and Java runtime for all profiles. Profiles can override it.
Touch button size, mouse speed, gyro and gamepad. The in-game layout itself is edited from the Controls button on the home screen.
Download source, updates, Discord presence — and Tutorials, where you can replay every guide.
The launcher language, including Hinglish and Hindi. The game keeps its own language setting.
